target.title: feat(azure): fork windows leases from snapshots
target.body:
## Summary

- add direct Azure Windows OS-disk checkpoints and snapshot-backed forks
- require explicit `--no-reboot=false`, deallocate for a consistent snapshot, then restart the source VM
- rotate SSH host keys, SSH login, Windows login, and TightVNC service credentials on each fork
- preserve loopback-only VNC and carry the snapshot subscription, resource group, region, and OS type into the fork
- reject ephemeral OS disks before deallocation and reject explicit managed-image requests instead of silently using snapshots
- document the disruptive checkpoint contract and managed-disk requirement

## Why

Prepared Azure Windows desktop leases are expensive to bootstrap repeatedly. A native OS-disk snapshot gives later leases a fast starting point, but only if the fork is treated as a new machine: identity and access credentials must rotate, VNC must remain tunnel-only, and Azure resource scope must follow the snapshot.

## Verification

Current landing candidate: `e685d7cc19b060d732103f19723ab4775eead404`, rebased onto current `main`.

- `go test ./internal/cli ./internal/providers/azure`
- `go vet ./...`
- exact-head CI: Go, Apple VZ, Worker, Scripts, Docs, and Release Check green
- whole-branch autoreview clean at 0.74 confidence after fixing two security findings: persisted desktop capability and deny-all fork quarantine until credential rotation completes
- regression coverage proves ephemeral disks are rejected before VM deallocation, desktop capability survives a fork without `--desktop`, and the quarantine NSG denies every inbound protocol

## Live Azure Proof

Exact-head proof on `e685d7cc19b060d732103f19723ab4775eead404`:

- Acquired source lease `cbx_f04d36a344b7` as an on-demand `Standard_D4s_v4` Azure Windows desktop; SSH and loopback VNC reached stable ready in 5m13.750s.
- Created managed OS-disk checkpoint `chk_b040883fb18bfe47`; Crabbox deallocated the source for consistency, created the snapshot, restarted the source, and observed the source ready again.
- Forked lease `cbx_366d974fa3bb` while intentionally omitting `--desktop`. Persisted source capability still selected desktop rehydration and reached stable SSH plus loopback VNC.
- Observed the fork NIC attached to its lease-scoped quarantine NSG with one priority-100 deny-all inbound rule while the specialized disk booted. Public SSH was blocked during this interval. After rehydration succeeded, the temporary NSG was gone and the NIC used the shared SSH allowlist.
- Verified all four fork credentials changed from the source: SSH login key, SSH host key, Windows password, and TightVNC password. Only hashes were compared locally; no credential material is recorded here.
- Verified public TCP 5900 remained blocked. An authenticated `crabbox screenshot` through the SSH-forwarded loopback VNC endpoint produced a clean Windows desktop locally; the image was not uploaded.
- Deleted fork, source, and checkpoint. Crabbox inventory returned empty, the checkpoint was absent, and Azure reported zero resources carrying either canary lease tag after deletion settled.

Maintainer acceptance: the documented bounded source deallocate/snapshot/restart lifecycle is acceptable for this feature.

## Stack

1. [https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/698](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/698) Azure Windows snapshot forks (this PR)
2. [#731](https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/731) Azure snapshot lifecycle performance
